title: Smooth source restriction identifies the sliced nearby-cycle comparison
statement:
Let $X\xrightarrow{h}Y\xrightarrow{g}S$ be finite-type morphisms, put $f=gh$, and suppose $h$ smooth on an open subscheme $W\subset X$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $\Lambda$ be finite killed by an integer invertible on $S$, and $M$ a finite $\Lambda$-module; write $\underline M$ for its constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For every base change $T\to S$, geometric specialization $b_T\to a_T$ over $b\to a$, and geometric $x_T\in W_{a_T}$ with image $y_T\in Y_{a_T}$, the ordinary comparison cones satisfy
$$C^f_T(\underline M)_{x_T}\simeq C^g_T(\underline M)_{y_T}.$$
Here $C$ denotes the sliced comparison cone on a geometric special fibre, as in [lem-trf-nearby-proper-source-exchange]; this assertion does not require $h$ proper. The isomorphism is compatible with further base changes. Also for every scheme $S$, $R\Psi_{1_S}\underline M\simeq p_2^*\underline M$, compatibly with arbitrary base change, so $(1_S,\underline M)$ is $\Psi$-good [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles].
